did_you_know.text: The first day of the seventh month is designated as a sacred assembly and a day of trumpet blasts, on which no ordinary work may be done.
The burnt offering for the first day consists of one bull, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs, all without defect.
The grain offerings for the first day vary according to the type of animal: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram, and one-tenth for each lamb.
The tenth day of the seventh month is set apart as a sacred assembly and a day of self-denial, on which no work may be done.
The burnt offering for the Day of Atonement is offered in addition to the sin offering of atonement, the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offerings.
The Feast of Booths begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and lasts seven days, each of which is a festival to the Lord.
On the first day of the Feast of Booths, thirteen bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs, all without defect, are offered.

The number of bulls offered during the Feast of Booths decreases each day—from thirteen on the first day to seven on the seventh—while the number of rams and lambs remains the same: two rams and fourteen lambs each day.
The eighth day is called a solemn assembly. It is a sacred assembly on which no ordinary work may be done, and its offering consists of one bull, one ram, and seven lambs.

The concluding verse emphasizes that the offerings for the appointed festivals are brought in addition to the vow offerings, freewill offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings.
